messages:
jin: heads up — after the 09:14 UTC deploy p99 ingest latency jumped ~18% for short payloads (seq len < 32). grafana: https://grafana.redwood/shot/abc123 — @ashley can you take a quick look?
ashley: looking now. waterfall points to host-proxy tokenization hotpath. flame graph top: tokenize_utf8_normalize -> minibuffer_writev -> syscall. quick perf stat: 
  token_parse_cpu: +42%
  writev_calls/sec: 12.3k -> 37.8k (canary)
  p99 short requests: 85ms -> 100ms
sam: fwiw we rolled a tiny change to the kernel_selector heuristics earlier (favours fast-small path). also there was an http2 lib upgrade in one service but we didn't think grpc paths hit it. could be an interaction (more small frames -> more writev).
jin: we didn't change grpc flags. timeline: kernel_selector tweak -> infra image -> deploy. I suspect the small-path kernel increases number of mini chunk outputs (more tiny frames) which amplifies write syscall overhead. command to revert locally: 
```
# revert kernel selector override
redwoodctl config set runtime.kernel_selector default-stable
redwoodctl deploy --canary 1%
```
ashley: also kvcache telemetry shows miss rate for short-context requests jumped: hit_rate short-ctx 87% -> 62% on canary. eviction churn up 3x. suggests tiny output bursts evicting hot shards.
sam: immediate mitigation ideas: bump kv shard prefetch and window to reduce eviction noise, and relax batching heuristic to accumulate up to 3ms or 4 tokens for tiny requests (trade small latency for much fewer syscalls). example patch: 
```
# runtime.conf snippet
batching.min_delay_ms = 3
batching.max_tokens_small = 4
kvcache.prefetch_shards = 128
```
leo: canary currently running 1% (20 hosts). metric blips: errors +0.8% and p99 regress +18% on those hosts. @canary-bot status pls.
canary-bot: Canary status: rollout paused automatically at 3% threshold. p50:+2.3%, p95:+4.1%, p99:+17.8% on canary cohort. Recent deploy id: d-2026-03-23-0914.
jin: plan: open small rollback PR for kernel_selector override + apply kvshard bump on canary. will also run microbench with --probe-tokenize to capture writev counts before/after.
ashley: if rollback not acceptable, I can prototype writev coalesce in host-proxy (aggregate tiny frames for 1ms window) — should drop writev_calls massively. will sketch a patch tonight.
sam: ops plan: (1) revert kernel_selector on canary (owned by sam), (2) apply kvcache.prefetch_shards=128 on same canary, (3) collect 10k request perf traces and flame graphs, (4) if p99 drops back <5% regressed, promote rollback.
jin: owning the perf traces & microbench. I'll attach sample trace and flame when done.
ashley: add unit test for kvcache eviction path — reproducer attached in PR should fail before fix.
sam: ok I'll kick the canary ops now. tagging action owners: @jin -> perf traces, @ashley -> host-proxy coalesce PR if needed, @sam -> canary rollout + revert.
leo: thx. ping here once canary shows green or we hit fallback.
